perf.summary: Replace the two byte-at-a-time zeroing loops over Keys and Values with a single bulk memclear.
perf.currentCost: Two scalar loops iterate keysSize and valuesSize BYTES individually (e.g. length*sizeof(TKey) iterations), each a load/store/branch. For length=10000 and 16-byte keys that is 160000 single-byte store iterations that Burst will not auto-collapse to wide stores because the loop bound is a runtime byte count and aliasing is opaque.
perf.proposedChange: Replace the `for (long i...) keysPtr[i]=0;` and the equivalent values loop with `Unsafe.InitBlockUnaligned(keysPtr, 0, (uint)keysSize)` (or a memset helper). Since the very next block also writes Next[i]=EmptyBucket in a separate loop, that loop is fine as-is (it writes int sentinels), but the two byte loops should be bulk clears.
perf.rationale: A single InitBlock/memset is implemented as wide vectorized stores (SIMD/`rep stos`) and is memory-bandwidth bound, vs. the current 1-byte-per-iteration loop which is branch/throughput bound at ~1 byte/cycle. Order of magnitude fewer retired instructions and far better store-port utilization.
perf.risk: Semantically identical (fills the same byte ranges with 0). keysSize/valuesSize already computed as long; cast to uint is safe only if a single allocation never exceeds 4GB — guard by clearing in a loop chunked to uint, or use a 64-bit memset helper. Otherwise none.

perf.summary: BucketCount is forced even (length*2 or 16) but bucket index uses %; make BucketCount a power of two and replace % with & (mask).
perf.currentCost: `(hashCode & 0x7FFFFFFF) % this.state->BucketCount` executes a hardware integer division (~20-40 cycle latency, not pipelined) on every insert during RecalculateBuckets (O(AllocatedLength) divisions) and on every TryGetFirstValue lookup.
perf.proposedChange: Round bucketCount up to the next power of two in SetAllocatedIndexLength (it is already a free-chosen `length*2`), store `bucketMask = bucketCount-1`, and compute `bucketIndex = hashCode & bucketMask` everywhere (drop the &0x7FFFFFFF since masking with a positive mask already yields a non-negative in-range index).
perf.rationale: AND is 1 cycle and fully pipelined vs. a multi-cycle non-pipelined DIV. On the hot lookup path and the O(n) rehash this removes the single most expensive instruction. Power-of-two bucket counts keep load factor identical (~2x slots).
perf.risk: Changes which bucket a key lands in, but observable map semantics (membership, value retrieval, iteration via Next chains) are unchanged. Must store the mask alongside or derive bucketCount-1; only valid because bucketCount is internally chosen, not caller-supplied.

perf.summary: Hoist this.state->Next into a local pointer before the probe loop to cut repeated double-indirection through state.
perf.currentCost: The probe loop reads `this.state->Next[entryIndex]` each iteration: a load of state->Next (pointer chase through state) plus the indexed load. keysPtr/valuesPtr are already hoisted but Next is not.
perf.proposedChange: Add `int* nextPtr = this.state->Next;` before the while loop and use `nextPtr[entryIndex]`. Same in TryGetNextValue and RecalculateBuckets.
perf.rationale: Removes one dependent load (state->Next) from the per-iteration dependency chain of a linked-list walk that is already latency-bound on cache misses; shortens the critical path.
perf.risk: None; state is not mutated inside the loop. Pure read hoist.

perf.summary: Specialize the byte-wise FNV hash and compare for common small power-of-two key sizes to avoid the per-byte loop.
perf.currentCost: HashKey loops sizeof(TKey) times with a dependent multiply chain (hash depends on previous hash) — for a 4- or 8-byte key that is 4-8 serialized iterations. CompareKeys does sizeof(TKey) byte compares with early-out branches; for an 8-byte key that is up to 8 branchy compares vs one 64-bit compare.
perf.proposedChange: In CompareKeys, when sizeof(TKey) is 4/8/16, do a single `*(uint*)`/`*(ulong*)` (or two ulong) equality test instead of the byte loop. sizeof(TKey) is a compile-time constant under Burst so the branch folds away. HashKey is harder to keep bit-identical, so leave its value semantics but consider it lower priority.
perf.rationale: Burst evaluates sizeof(TKey) at compile time, so the size-dispatch is free and only the matching widened-compare path is emitted: one 64-bit compare replaces an 8-iteration branchy loop, cutting both instruction count and mispredict risk on the hot lookup path.
perf.risk: CompareKeys with widened loads is bit-identical to byte compare for blittable keys (no padding concerns since the same bytes are compared). Do NOT change HashKey's arithmetic if any persisted/cross-call hash identity is assumed; the bucket mapping is internal so a different-but-consistent hash is acceptable, but keep it deterministic.
